decisionMemo.businessProblem: A profitable $25M D2C apparel brand growing ~30% YoY faces decelerating domestic acquisition (paid CAC +35% over 18 months, active-buyer growth down to ~12%) and a finite domestic TAM at its price point. To sustain growth toward ~$50M it must choose its next primary expansion market within 90 days, funded from a capped ~$8-10M non-dilutive budget and constrained by a near-full domestic warehouse, no in-house international operations, and unproven fit of its sizing and positioning abroad. Three options compete: (A) deepen the proven domestic market (lowest execution risk but limited remaining TAM), (B) enter Europe (larger addressable TAM, demonstrated organic pull in 3 countries, but higher benchmarked CAC and unproven localized economics), or (C) enter Asia (largest absolute interest and TAM, but elevated return/sizing risk and operational/regulatory complexity). The central question is which expansion's unit economics and operational fit are most defensible given what is actually known, versus what must be tested before any irreversible merchandising and fulfillment commitments are locked.

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually
